answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before earning reputation, then slash that stake when independently sampled interactions reveal fabricated identities coordinating to trade with themselves. A real participant risks losing funds through misconduct, while an attacker must lock fresh capital for every sybil and keep it exposed throughout the audit window. That makes a fake-agent garden costly to scale across a knoll or ridge, especially when identities cannot share one stake.
